name: Seeed reTerminal Sticky
description: ePaper reader, ESP32-S3, driven in the panel's 4-level grayscale mode. The controller scans 800x480 landscape and the glass is mounted at 90 degrees, so the firmware transposes on the device and the server renders ordinary 480x800 portrait. Pairs with the tesserae-device-firmware build that declares this kind at register, and speaks Tesserae's v1 REST device API. Server-side pack via esp32_gray2_bin produces a raw 2-bpp 4-level grayscale buffer (96000 bytes) the firmware paints without any on-device decode.
notes_md:
The only Sticky kind. Confirmed on real hardware running the tesserae-device-firmware build for this board. Wire format is exactly 96000 bytes (800*480/4), row-major from top-left, 4 pixels per byte MSB first (bits 7-6 = leftmost pixel), 2-bit value 0b00 = black, 0b11 = white, linear 4-level gray; no header, no padding, no checksum. Byte-identical to `seeed_reterminal_e1001_gray`, so the renderer and packer are shared unchanged.

`orientation` is `portrait`, pinned on hardware rather than inferred: a test frame of four grey bands with a white corner marker painted with the bands running top to bottom, black first, and the marker in the top-left, confirming both axes. Getting this wrong is a 180-degree error, so change it only against a real unit.

Supersedes `seeed_sticky` and `seeed_sticky_gray`, retired in v0.344.0. Those described the same hardware running CrossInk, were derived from the V01 schematic and Seeed's vendor demo rather than a validated unit, and declared a provisional `portrait_flipped` this board does not use. A kind is also an OTA lineage (release descriptors are signed with a `device_kind` and rejected on mismatch), so a second firmware would need its own kind again rather than a variant of this one. `migrate_retired_sticky_kinds` moves any instance still on the old ids.

`auto_select: false` because this SKU is indistinguishable on the wire from `xteink_x4_gray`: same protocol, same gamut, same 480x800 geometry, same 96000 bytes. A device running this firmware names its own kind at register and discover, so nothing is lost there, but relay pairing infers a SKU from the wire signature instead of reading a declared kind, and this id sorts ahead of `xteink_x4_gray` in that tie-break. Without this flag an Xteink X4 pairing over a relay would be relabelled a reTerminal Sticky.
